examples.text: We packed **ahead of time**, so the morning was calm.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Arrive **ahead of time** for the interview.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "ahead of the time"
wrong.text: I reached ahead of the time.

meaning: Move or act fast because time is short.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: **Hurry**, the bus leaves in five minutes!

examples.label: At work
examples.text: No need to **hurry**; the client is late too.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: We had to **hurry** to catch the train.

wrong.label: ✗ Needs "a" as a noun
wrong.text: I am in hurry.

rule: hurry up; be in a hurry

meaning: Taking a lot of time.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: Checking every invoice by hand is **time-consuming**.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Making biryani is **time-consuming** but worth it.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Filling in this form is very **time-consuming**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for people
wrong.text: My manager is time-consuming.

meaning: Never ending, or happening again and again.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: There's a **perpetual** traffic jam outside our building.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: He's in a **perpetual** hurry, even on Sundays.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: The office printer is a **perpetual** problem.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for something that happened once
wrong.text: I had a perpetual cold last Tuesday.

meaning: Any day from Monday to Friday.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: On a **weekday**, I wake up at six.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: The mall is quiet on a **weekday** morning.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: The shop is open every **weekday** till nine.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for Saturday or Sunday
wrong.text: Sunday is my favourite weekday.

meaning: Do something to pass time while you wait.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: We played cards to **kill time** at the airport.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I scroll my phone to **kill time** in the queue.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: We got there early, so we walked around to **kill time**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for saving time
wrong.text: Take the metro to kill time; it's faster.

meaning: Two weeks.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: My parents are visiting for a **fortnight**.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: We'll send the report every **fortnight**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: I'll be back in a **fortnight**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for a few days
wrong.text: We stayed a fortnight, just Friday to Monday.

meaning: Have no time left.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: We always **run out of time** in these meetings.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Start packing now, or we'll **run out of time**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Don't spend too long on one question, or you'll **run out of time**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "of the time"
wrong.text: We ran out of the time.

options.text: We ran out of the time.

meaning: Lasting a very short time.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: We had a **fleeting** chat at the wedding.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: There was a **fleeting** moment of quiet before the kids woke up.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: I caught a **fleeting** look at the actor.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for long things
wrong.text: It was a fleeting ten-year job.

meaning: During the night.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Soak the beans **overnight**.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: We took a bus **overnight** to Goa.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Leave the phone charging **overnight**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for a whole week
wrong.text: We stayed overnight for seven days.

meaning: Find time for something, even when busy.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I always **make time** for my kids' school play.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: Can you **make time** for a quick call today?

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Try to **make time** for a walk every day.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "do time"
wrong.text: Can you do time for me today?

rule: make time for something or someone

meaning: In the last few days or weeks.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Have you seen any good films **lately**?

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I've been sleeping badly **lately**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Prices have gone up a lot **lately**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for "late"
wrong.text: I came lately to work today.

rule: lately = recently; late = after the time

meaning: Time when you are not working.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: I'm taking some **time off** after the launch.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We'll visit Grandma when I get **time off**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: She needs **time off** to rest.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for time at work
wrong.text: I had time off all day in meetings.

meaning: About to happen very soon.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: The launch is **imminent**; everyone is on standby.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Look at those dark clouds; rain is **imminent**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: With the exam **imminent**, she studied all night.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "eminent" (famous)
wrong.text: He is an imminent doctor.

meaning: These days; at the present time.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: **Nowadays** everyone pays by phone.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Kids **nowadays** know more about phones than we do.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: **Nowadays** I work from home twice a week.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for the past
wrong.text: Nowadays, back in 1990, we wrote letters.

meaning: At a quieter, often cheaper time.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We shop at **off-peak** hours to skip the queues.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: **Off-peak** train tickets are much cheaper.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: We go to the gym at **off-peak** times to avoid the crowds.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for the busiest time
wrong.text: Rush hour is off-peak.

meaning: At the same time, while something else happens.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The rice is cooking. **Meanwhile**, cut the onions.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: IT is fixing the server; **meanwhile**, use the backup.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: I'll call the plumber. **Meanwhile**, turn off the tap.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for "after a long time"
wrong.text: He finally came back meanwhile.

options.text: The tea is brewing. Meanwhile, set the table.

meaning: The busy time when people go to or from work.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Don't drive in **rush hour**; it takes forever.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: The metro is packed during **rush hour**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Let's leave at four to beat the **rush hour**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for a quiet time
wrong.text: At 2 a.m. the roads are full of rush hour.

meaning: Happening now and then, not regularly.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We get **sporadic** power cuts in summer.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: His replies are **sporadic**, so call him instead.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: There was only **sporadic** rain this monsoon.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for something regular
wrong.text: My sporadic gym visits are every day at six.

meaning: Up to now.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: **So far**, the client is happy.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: How's the new job **so far**?

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: We've saved 20,000 **so far** this year.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for a finished past time
wrong.text: So far, I went to Goa in 2019.

options.text: So far, I've read two chapters.
So far, I read two chapters in 2010.
So far I will read two chapters.

meaning: All day and all night.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: The team worked **round the clock** to fix the bug.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The hospital canteen is open **round the clock**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: The pharmacy near us is open **round the clock**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for a few hours
wrong.text: The shop is open round the clock, ten to six.

meaning: Early enough, before it's too late.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We reached the station just **in time**.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: Will the report be ready **in time** for Monday?

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: I got home **in time** to see the match.

wrong.label: ✗ Not when you were too late
wrong.text: We missed the train, but we were in time.

meaning: Sometimes, not often.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: We meet for coffee **every now and then**.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: **Every now and then** I cook for the whole family.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: I check my savings **every now and then**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for every day
wrong.text: I brush my teeth every now and then, twice a day.

check.question: What does every now and then mean?

meaning: Lasting only a short time.

examples.label: Explain your thinking
examples.text: The price jump is **transient**; it will settle next month.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The pain was **transient**; it went away in minutes.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Bad moods are **transient**, so don't decide anything now.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for things that last
wrong.text: They had a transient marriage of fifty years.

meaning: The latest possible time.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: He always sends the slides at the **last minute**.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We packed at the **last minute** and forgot the charger.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Don't leave the shopping till the **last minute**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for early
wrong.text: I booked a month ahead, at the last minute.

rule: at the last minute = very late

meaning: For now, but not forever.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We're staying with my parents **for the time being**.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: Use the old laptop **for the time being**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: **For the time being**, let's keep it simple.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for forever
wrong.text: I'll live here for the time being, for the rest of my life.

options.text: For the time being, I was born in 1990.
Use my pen for the time being.
I'll love you for the time being, forever.

meaning: A very long time (casual).

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: I haven't seen you in **ages**!

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The queue at the bank took **ages**.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: It's been **ages** since we went to the movies.

wrong.label: ✗ Not in formal writing
wrong.text: Dear Sir, your reply took ages.

meaning: Sometimes, not often.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We order pizza **once in a while**.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Call your parents **once in a while**!

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: **Once in a while**, I take the long way home.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for "only once"
wrong.text: I went to Paris once in a while, in 2015.

meaning: Earned with a lot of work.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Don't waste your **hard-earned** money on that.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: She spent her **hard-earned** bonus on her parents.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: We used our **hard-earned** savings for the house.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for money you did not work for
wrong.text: My lottery win is hard-earned.

options.text: Money from a year of overtime.

meaning: Some time, not very long or very short.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Wait **a while**; she's on her way.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: It's been **a while** since we visited Grandma.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: I'll rest for **a while** and then start.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "since a while"
wrong.text: I'm waiting since a while.

rule: for a while; after a while

meaning: Lasting only for a short time.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: It's a **temporary** job for the summer.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: This is a **temporary** fix until the plumber comes.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: The road is closed, but it's **temporary**.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "temporarily" before a noun
wrong.text: It's a temporarily job.

meaning: Happening once a year.

examples.label: At work
examples.text: Our **annual** review is in March.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The **annual** school fee is due in April.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: The **annual** family trip is my favourite week.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for every month
wrong.text: The annual electricity bill comes every month.

meaning: Happening sometimes, not often.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I enjoy the **occasional** sweet after dinner.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: We have the **occasional** movie night.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: There may be **occasional** delays on this route.

wrong.label: ✗ Not after a verb
wrong.text: I occasional go to the gym.

meaning: Too careful with money, in a mean way.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: He's so **penny-pinching** he won't share a taxi.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Our **penny-pinching** landlord won't fix the fan.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Stop being **penny-pinching**; it's her birthday.

wrong.label: ✗ Not praise
wrong.text: My penny-pinching mum kindly bought us all gifts.

rule: penny-pinching is not a compliment; thrifty is

meaning: Low in price.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Vegetables are **cheap** at the weekly market.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: That hotel is **cheap** but very clean.

right.label: ✓ Use it right
right.text: Buses are **cheap** and run every ten minutes.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for prices
wrong.text: The price is cheap.

rule: things are cheap; prices are low
